ai.description: *Cnemaspis goaensis* is a small gecko (SVL ~35 mm) with a brown body, yellow-spotted flanks, and a pale vertebral stripe. It features keeled ventral scales and a distinctively slender, elongated tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis goaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Goan Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests, typically found on tree trunks or rocky outcrops at low to moderate elevations in the Western Ghats.
ai.behavior: The Goan Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis goaensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis goaensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats, specifically occurring in the states of Goa and Karnataka at elevations between 100 and 800 meters.
